levels.name: Poorly
levels.description: The child is not doing well in his house: underfed, unsettled, and you are frightened for it.

levels.name: Fretful
levels.description: The child is fretful and going short, and you lie awake counting what it lacks.

levels.name: Settled
levels.description: The child is settled: fed, warm and sleeping, and wanting for nothing that matters.

levels.name: Thriving
levels.description: The child is thriving in his house: growing fast, sleeping well, quick to smile.

levels.name: Blooming
levels.description: The child is blooming: the healthiest, happiest baby you have ever seen, and the whole house dotes on it.

texts.offer: {player}, good morning. Una Fairweather, Sire Relations Office. I understand congratulations are in order, and so the Office's housing scheme is open to you. For the file, the terms: {house}, a secure family house on Quince Row, with a nanny of ours living in. The rent is {rent} on the first of each month, which is the subsidised rate. You would give up your room in the Halls. You may build onto the house and fit it out at your own cost, and the mothers of your children may live there with you. Tell me whether you will take it.
texts.welcome: The keys to {house} are logged to you as of this hour, and the wards know you. Your first rent of {rent} falls due on the first of next month. Rent not paid is carried for seven days and no longer. Zélie Marchand, your nanny, is already in the house. Welcome home, {player}.
texts.nannyHello: Bonjour, monsieur. Zélie. I come with the house, non? Your room is aired, there is coffee, and I have put the bassinet where no draught will find it. Come home when you like. The door knows you now, and so do I.
texts.arrears: {player}, for the file: this month's rent on {house} was not met. {amount} is now owing. It must be paid by {date}, or the Office takes the house back and everyone in it goes home. I would rather not write that letter. Pay it from the house's own accounts.
texts.paid: Received, {amount}. The file on {house} is in order again. Thank you for seeing to it.
texts.evicted: {player}, the rent on {house} went unpaid past the days of grace, and the Office has taken the house back as of this morning. Your room in the Halls has been kept. I am sorry it came to this. There will not be a second offer.

rooms.name: The hearth room
rooms.description: The room one comes into: a kitchen and a living room in one, with a long table, a stove that is never quite cold, and the front door at one end with its ward-plate and its log.

tiers.name: A proper kitchen
tiers.description: The kitchen has been fitted out properly: a range, a deep sink, a pantry that is kept full.

rooms.name: The family room
rooms.description: A sitting room for the whole house: deep sofas, a rug to lie on, shelves of games and picture books, and room for everyone at once.

rooms.name: The study
rooms.description: A small quiet room with a desk under the window, a good lamp and a door that shuts.

tiers.name: The reading wall
tiers.description: One whole wall is books now, with the set texts of every course he takes and a ladder to reach them.

rooms.name: The nanny's room
rooms.description: The nanny's own room, off the hearth room and next to where a nursery goes: a narrow bed made with hospital corners, a dressing table with its mirror, and a listening-charm on the sill.

rooms.name: The nursery
rooms.description: A nursery with three cots, a changing table, a rocking chair, and wards on the window that hum very slightly.

tiers.name: The night nursery
tiers.description: It has been made over into a proper night nursery: two more cots, a bed for whoever sits up, a stove of its own and a lamp that never quite goes out.

rooms.name: The garden
rooms.description: A walled garden behind the house: a lawn, a quince tree, beds somebody has to weed, and a bench in the sun.

tiers.name: The glasshouse
tiers.description: A glasshouse stands against the south wall, warm in any weather, with a table and two chairs among the plants.

rooms.name: The master bedroom
rooms.description: His own room: a wide bed, a wardrobe, a window over the garden, and a bassinet in the corner that came with the house.

tiers.name: The household bed
tiers.description: The bed has been replaced with one built for more than two, as the Office catalogue puts it without blushing.

rooms.name: The bathroom
rooms.description: A plain bathroom with a deep old tub and a mirror that steams over.

tiers.name: The bath suite
tiers.description: It has been knocked through into a bath suite: a sunken tub big enough for company, warm stone underfoot, and hot water that does not run out.

rooms.name: The west bedroom
rooms.description: A bedroom at the back of the house with a window seat, for someone to make her own.

rooms.name: The east bedroom
rooms.description: A bedroom that gets the morning sun, for someone to make her own.

rooms.name: The attic room
rooms.description: A long room under the roof with sloping ceilings and a round window, private and a little apart from the rest of the house.
